devdoc.details: This contract serves as the primary interface for campaign creators and provides helper functions for APIs built on MerklDeprecated variables are maintained in storage for upgrade compatibility

AdminChanged(address,address).details: Emitted when the admin account has changed.

BeaconUpgraded(address).details: Emitted when the beacon is changed.

Initialized(uint8).details: Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized.

Upgraded(address).details: Emitted when the implementation is upgraded.

acceptConditions().details: If the conditions change (through setMessage), users must accept again the new termsIf the messageHash is not set, it means that there are no conditions to accept

campaign(bytes32).details: Returns original parameters even if the campaign has been overridden

params._campaignId: ID of the campaign to retrieve

campaignId((bytes32,address,address,uint.details: Campaign ID is computed as keccak256 of creator, rewardToken, campaignType, startTimestamp, duration, and campaignData

returns._0: Unique campaign ID derived from hashing key parameters

campaignLookup(bytes32).details: Reverts if the campaign does not exist

params._campaignId: ID of the campaign to look up

returns._0: Zero-based index of the campaign in the campaignList array

createCampaign((bytes32,address,address,.details: Campaigns with invalid formatting may not be processed by the reward engine, potentially losing rewardsReward tokens must be whitelisted and amounts must exceed the token-specific minimum thresholdReverts if the sender has not accepted the terms and conditions via acceptConditions()

params.newCampaign: Parameters defining the campaign structure and rewards

returns._0: campaignId Unique identifier for the newly created campaign

params.campaigns: Array of campaign parameters to create

returns._0: Array of campaign IDs for all newly created campaigns

decreaseTokenAllowance(address,address,a.details: Only callable by the user themselves or a governor

params.amount: Amount to decrease the allowance by
params.operator: Operator whose allowance is being reduced
params.rewardToken: Token for which allowance is reduced

decreaseTokenBalance(address,address,add.details: Only callable by the user themselves or a governor

params.to: Address that will receive the withdrawn tokens
params.user: Address whose balance will be decreased

returns._0: Array of addresses that had rewards reallocated away from them
Address at the specified index that had rewards reallocated away
Array of block timestamps when overrides occurred

getLatestCampaignParams(bytes32).details: If an override exists (non-zero campaignId), returns the override; otherwise returns original campaignEven if an override is invalid, we return the latest override data. This is safe because invalid overrides result in the campaign being parsed as invalid by the Merkl engine

params._campaignId: ID of the campaign to retrieve

returns._0: Campaign parameters with overrides applied if they exist, otherwise original parameters

getValidRewardTokens().details: Not optimized for onchain queries; intended for off-chain/API use

returns._0: Array of reward tokens with their minimum amounts per epoch

getValidRewardTokens(uint32,uint32).details: Not optimized for onchain queries; intended for off-chain/API use

params.first: Maximum number of tokens to return

returns._0: Array of reward tokens and total count

increaseTokenAllowance(address,address,a.details: Only callable by the user themselves or a governor

params.amount: Amount to increase the allowance by
params.rewardToken: Token for which allowance is granted

increaseTokenBalance(address,address,uin.details: When called by a governor, the user MUST have sent tokens to the contract beforehandCan be used to deposit on behalf of another userWARNING: Do not use with any non strictly standard ERC20 (like rebasing tokens) as they will cause accounting issues

params.user: Address whose balance will be increased

params._accessControlManager: Address of the access control manager contract
params._fees: Default fee rate in base 10^9 (must be less than BASE_9)

overrideCampaign(bytes32,(bytes32,addres.details: Cannot change rewardToken, amount, or creator addressThe Merkl engine validates overrides and rejects invalid modifications, including attempts to circumvent campaign-specific fee ratesThe rejection of invalid modifications leads to the campaign being parsed as invalid and the leftover reward tokens allocated to the campaign creator addressInvalid overrides may result in the campaign not being processed while fees are still deducted

params._campaignId: ID of the campaign to override
params.newCampaign: New campaign parameters (some fields will be ignored or validated)

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

reallocateCampaignRewards(bytes32,addres.details: Can only be called after the campaign has ended (startTimestamp + duration has passed)Reallocation validity is determined by the Merkl engine; invalid reallocations are ignored

params._campaignId: ID of the completed campaign to reallocate from
params.froms: Array of addresses whose unclaimed rewards should be reallocated
params.to: Address that will receive the reallocated rewards

recover(address,address,uint256).details: Only callable by governorWARNING: Be extremely careful not to withdraw tokens that have been predeposited by users via increaseTokenBalanceWithdrawing predeposited user tokens will break the accounting system and cause loss of funds for usersThis function should only be used to recover tokens accidentally sent to the contract or accumulated protocol feesAlways verify that the amount being recovered does not exceed fees and does not include user predeposits

params.to: Address that will receive the recovered tokens

setCampaignFees(uint32,uint256).details: Only callable by governor or guardianSet fee to 1 to effectively waive fees for a campaign typeFee rate must be less than BASE_9 (100%)

params._fees: Fee rate for this campaign type in base 10^9

setFees(uint256).details: Only callable by governor or guardianFee rate must be less than BASE_9 (100%)

params._defaultFees: New default fee rate in base 10^9

setMessage(string).details: Only callable by governor or guardianAutomatically computes and stores the keccak256 hashThe message may be a link to the full terms hosted offchain

params._message: New terms and conditions message text

setNewDistributor(address).details: Only callable by governorThis function is not meant to be used and mostly kept here to help with testing

setRewardTokenMinAmounts(address[],uint2.details: Only callable by governor or guardianSetting amount to 0 effectively removes the token from the whitelistPrevents duplicate entries when adding previously removed tokensWARNING: Non-standard tokens (e.g., tokens with fee-on-transfer, rebasing tokens) must not be whitelisted as they break the Merkl accounting logic

params.amounts: Array of minimum amounts (0 = remove from whitelist, >0 = add/update)

setUserFeeRebate(address,uint256).details: Only callable by governor or guardian

params.user: User address receiving the fee rebate

toggleCampaignOperator(address,address).details: Only callable by the user themselves or a governorToggles between authorized (1) and unauthorized (0)

params.operator: Operator whose authorization is being toggled
params.user: User granting or revoking operator access

toggleSigningWhitelist(address).details: Only callable by governor or guardianWhitelisted users (status = 1) can create campaigns without accepting Merkl terms

params.user: User address whose whitelist status is being toggled

upgradeTo(address).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes).details: Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `newImplementation`, and subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`. Calls {_authorizeUpgrade}. Emits an {Upgraded} event.

__gap.details: This empty reserved space is put in place to allow future versions to add new variables without shifting down storage in the inheritance chain. See https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/4.x/upgradeable#storage_gaps

campaignList.details: This list can grow unbounded, but is only accessed by view functions

messageHash.details: The message may be a link to the full terms hosted offchain

rewardTokenMinAmounts.details: A value of 0 indicates the token is not whitelisted and cannot be used as a reward

userSignatureWhitelist.details: The name includes 'signature' for legacy reasons, reflecting the original requirement for users to sign conditions

userSignatures.details: The name includes 'signature' for legacy reasons, reflecting the original requirement for users to sign conditions
